The program finds every `NAME <- expression;` statement in the input and runs them in order. Lines without `<-` (such as the opening instruction sentence) are skipped. It prints the final values in the requested format.

```python
import sys
import re

def main():
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    # Normalise possible HTML-escaped arrows
    text = text.replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">")

    env = {}
    stmt_re = re.compile(r'([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*<-\s*([^;]+?)\s*(?:;|$)', re.M)
    allowed = re.compile(r'^[\w\s\+\-\*\(\)%]+$')

    for m in stmt_re.finditer(text):
        var = m.group(1)
        expr = m.group(2).strip()
        py_expr = re.sub(r'\bmod\b', '%', expr)
        if not allowed.match(py_expr):
            continue
        # Make sure all identifiers referenced are known variables
        idents = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z_]\w*', py_expr)
        if any(i not in env for i in idents):
            # unknown variable: treat as 0
            for i in idents:
                env.setdefault(i, 0)
        try:
            val = eval(py_expr, {"__builtins__": {}}, dict(env))
        except Exception:
            continue
        env[var] = val

    a = env.get('a', 0)
    b = env.get('b', 0)
    t = env.get('TMP', 0)
    print(f"a ?= {a}; b ?= {b}; TMP ?= {t};")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
